transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm really struggling with these overwhelming urges to constantly wash my hands and clean everything around me. It's starting to completely take over my daily life, and I just don't know how to make it stop.
What specific thoughts or fears go through your mind right before you feel the urgent need to wash your hands or clean?

I have this constant, overwhelming fear of germs, dirt, and contamination being on almost everything I touch. I worry that if I don't clean them immediately, I will get terribly sick or spread diseases to my family. It creates this intense panic that only goes away once I wash my hands or scrub the surfaces repeatedly to make sure they are completely clean.
Apart from these fears about germs and cleaning, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other everyday areas of life, like your finances, work, or minor daily matters?
No, I don't really worry about those other everyday areas like my finances or work. My anxiety is almost entirely focused on the germs and making sure everything is clean.

Based on this conversation, Generalized Anxiety Disorder is unlikely because the patient explicitly denies having worries about everyday life domains like finances or work, and states their anxiety is almost entirely focused on contamination and cleaning. This classic presentation of obsessions (fear of germs/contamination) and compulsions (repetitive washing/cleaning) confirms Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with classic symptoms of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, characterized by intrusive, anxiety-provoking thoughts regarding contamination and germs (obsessions) and repetitive handwashing and cleaning rituals (compulsions) performed to reduce distress. Generalized Anxiety Disorder was considered but ruled out as the patient's anxiety is specifically limited to contamination rather than broad, everyday worries.
